newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police nab 51 Chinese for illegal entry.
newsitem.headline: Japan police nab 51 Chinese for illegal entry.

text.p: Japanese authorities on Monday arrested 51 Chinese and three Japanese on illegal immigration charges, while a hunt was continuing for another group thought to have landed on Sunday, a maritime official said.
The arrest is the latest in a series of hauls of Chinese illegal immigrants in Japan and has sparked worries of growing ties between Chinese and Japanese gangsters in smuggling refugees.
Maritime Safety Agency (MSA) officials seized the 200-tonne "Johaiyu" with 51 Chinese -- 44 men and 7 women -- on board on Sunday night.
"We have arrested all 51 Chinese on board, none of whom were carrying passports," an MSA official said.

He said the boat was first spotted off the main southern island of Kyushu last Thursday when it was followed until being boarded on Sunday night. It was then taken into the port city of Nagoya in central Japan.
A Nagoya police spokesman said the three arrested Japanese were accused of abetting illegal immigration.
"The three Japanese were arrested after we found them waiting with two trucks at Nagoya port, apparently ready to take the Chinese away," he said.
Police also continued a search for around 50 Chinese nationals they suspect disembarked at a secluded cove in southern Honshu, the main Japanese island, early on Sunday morning.
Earlier this month, Japan's Foreign Ministry formally asked Beijing to step up patrols along Chinese coastlines and to crack down on Chinese brokers profiting from the smuggling trade.

The request follows a recent rise in the number of Chinese nationals trying to enter Japan illegally. In the past two months alone Japan took 330 Chinese nationals into custody for attempting to enter Japan illegally, the government said.
Last year, police reported a record 29 cases of illegal entry in groups. Of the 679 people taken into custody, 545 were identified as Chinese, according to National Police Agency statistics.
Those caught by police constantly refer to Snakeheads, professional Chinese brokers feared for their viciousness, as being behind the trade in human cargo.
